title: The rosary story
hookLine: tradition says Dominic received the rosary; historians say it grew over a long time, much loved by Dominicans

lines: A WOMAN IN BLUE, A KNEELING FRIAR.
SHE HANDS HIM A STRING OF BEADS.
cards: It's in paintings, in stained glass, above side altars. A woman in blue, crowned, sits with a child on her lap. Kneeling below her is a friar in a white habit and a black cape.
She leans down and hands him a string of beads. The friar is Dominic, the woman is Mary, and the beads are a rosary. It's a beautiful scene, and Dominicans have painted it lovingly.
It also raises a question a curious person will eventually ask: did it happen like that? Today, the rosary story, and why the answer comes in two parts.

teach.h: TRADITION: MARY GIVES DOMINIC THE BEADS.
teach.b: Back on day four, you met what the rosary's string is for; today, its story. Part one is the tradition. Tradition says Mary gave the rosary to Dominic, as a help for his preaching in the south of France.
Popes and preachers have retold it, and the picture hangs in Dominican churches.

teach.h: HISTORY: A PRAYER THAT GREW SLOWLY.
teach.b: Part two is what historians see: a prayer that grew slowly, from many hands. Monks prayed the Psalms. People who couldn't read them prayed Our Fathers instead, counted on strings of beads or knots.

teach.h: THE HAIL MARY BEGINS IN LUKE.
teach.b: Then came the Hail Mary, whose first lines are two greetings from Luke's Gospel stitched together. Gabriel's, in the Douay-Rheims: "Hail, full of grace, the Lord is with thee: blessed art thou among women."

And Elizabeth's, when Mary visits her: "blessed is the fruit of thy womb." Over time people attached scenes to the beads, moments in the lives of Jesus and Mary to think about while the words went by: the mysteries.

teach.h: DOMINICANS LOVED IT AND SPREAD IT.
teach.b: And the Dominicans? Historians credit them with loving and spreading the rosary widely, preaching it and gathering people to pray it together; a later Dominican preacher also spread the story of Dominic receiving it.
So Catholics hold this in different ways.
Some take the story as history. Others read it as a picture of something true: the rosary found its home among Dominicans.
Either way, the prayer grew like a family recipe, a pinch added by each generation, until nobody can say whose it was. It belongs to all of them.

how: Catholics pray the rosary alone or together, often on beads, saying an Our Father, a decade of Hail Marys and a Glory Be while meditating on a mystery; Dominican friars and parishes lead it and preach about it.

games.q: you can't read, so you can't pray the Psalms the way the monks do. you still want a daily prayer with a steady rhythm. what do you do?
o: give up: prayer is for people who can read.
pray Our Fathers, counting them on a string of beads.
pay a monk to pray for you.
games.why: historians see this as one of the roots of the rosary: simple prayers counted on beads or knots. the Hail Mary and the mysteries came later.

practice: Hold a rosary if you have one, or use your fingers.

If you pray, say an Our Father, a Hail Mary for each bead or finger, then a Glory Be, holding one scene in mind the whole time, Gabriel coming to Mary; if not, let each finger be one slow breath under the same scene: a young woman, a visitor, a word of greeting.

wordCard.voice: The rosary story. Tradition says Mary gave it to Dominic; historians see a prayer that grew slowly, loved and spread by Dominicans. Today's word.

orig.note: Latin: a rose garden. the prayer's name pictures a garland of prayers offered to Mary.

carryVoice: Your line: a story that grew. Many hands, one string of beads, and room for every way of holding it. Back tomorrow, same hill.
